summary: Closed the snapshot-retention lead I checked this turn: it looked as though a store with no retained snapshots would let FileSnapshotSink.Close reap the snapshot it had just finalized — before takeSnapshot recorded it and compacted the logs below it — leaving a node with neither logs nor a snapshot, but the constructor rejects that configuration (NewFileSnapshotStoreWithLogger errors when retain is below one and the public constructor delegates to it), so at least the newest snapshot always survives and reaping walks a newest-first list. Only the source range was recorded; no claim was made because nothing new was established. I also stated the next step I intend rather than leaving it implicit: the verify account's remaining limitation is that the caller's FSM read is never exercised, so its stale-read consequence is argued from the endpoint and the concurrent successor. A probe can show it end to end by committing a value before the partition, letting the successor commit a different value, and reading the stalled leader's FSM after its verify returns success — that is what I would build with the remaining run time.
